#+title: Feature Module Format

Each feature is a single =.nix= file in =dotfiles/dot_config/nix/modules/features/=.
Files are auto-discovered by =feature-loader.nix= via =builtins.readDir= and imported as
*recipes* (plain attrsets). All HM-module boilerplate is generated by the loader.

* Recipe Format (primary)

A recipe is a plain Nix file returning an attrset — no =options=, no =config=, no =mkIf=:

#+begin_src nix
{ pkgs, lib, user ? { }, ... }:
{
  description = "Helix editor + marksman LSP";
  category    = "editor";

  # defaultEnable = true;   # optional: enable by default (mise, nix-system)

  packages = {
    nix        = with pkgs; [ helix marksman ];   # all platforms
    linux.nix  = with pkgs; [ ... ];              # Linux-only packages
    darwin.casks      = [ "some-app" ];           # Homebrew casks
    darwin.taps       = [ "owner/tap" ];          # Homebrew taps
    darwin.brews      = [ { name = "formula"; } ];# Homebrew brews (attrsets)
    darwin.brewBundle = ''brew "formula"'';       # extraConfig string
  };

  activation.darwin = {
    scriptName = ''shell text'';   # darwin activation script body
  };

  # Escape hatch for HM-specific options (home.activation, fonts.fontconfig, etc.)
  hmConfig = { config, lib, pkgs, isDarwin, isLinux }:
    lib.optionalAttrs isDarwin {
      home.activation.someEntry =
        lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" ] ''echo "setup"'';
    };

  bump   = { before = [...]; run = [...]; capture = [...]; };
  update = [ { run = [...]; onFailure = "warn"; } ];
}
#+end_src

* Recipe fields

| Field              | Type       | Description                                               |
|--------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------|
| =description=      | string     | Human-readable label shown in =kaizen configure= wizard   |
| =category=         | string     | Group key (=editor=, =dev=, =terminal=, =system=, ...)    |
| =defaultEnable=    | bool       | Enable by default without user opt-in (false if omitted)  |
| =packages.nix=     | list       | nixpkgs packages for all platforms                        |
| =packages.linux.nix= | list     | nixpkgs packages for Linux only                           |
| =packages.darwin.casks= | list  | Homebrew casks                                            |
| =packages.darwin.taps= | list   | Homebrew taps                                             |
| =packages.darwin.brews= | list  | Homebrew brews (attrsets with name, restart_service, …)   |
| =packages.darwin.brewBundle= | str | Raw =extraConfig= lines for brew bundle             |
| =activation.darwin= | attrs    | Darwin activation scripts (name → shell text)             |
| =activation.linux= | attrs    | Linux activation scripts (name → shell text)              |
| =hmConfig=         | function   | Escape hatch: returns HM module attrset for complex needs |
| =bump=             | attrset    | Bump workflow: =before=, =run=, =capture=                 |
| =update=           | list       | Update hooks run by =kaizen update=                       |

* =hmConfig= escape hatch

When a feature needs HM-specific options that do not fit the recipe keys
(e.g. =fonts.fontconfig.enable=, =programs.*=, multi-entry =home.activation=),
use the =hmConfig= function:

#+begin_src nix
hmConfig = { config, lib, pkgs, isDarwin, isLinux }:
  lib.optionalAttrs isLinux {
    fonts.fontconfig.enable = true;
  };
#+end_src

The function receives =config= (current HM config), =lib=, =pkgs=, =isDarwin=,
=isLinux= and returns a plain attrset merged into the recipe's enabled block.

* Stub files

Return an empty attrset to tell the loader to skip a file entirely:

#+begin_src nix
# darkman.nix — real config is in modules/system/darkman.nix
{ ... }: { }
#+end_src

* macOS deps (darwin JSON-bridge)

Darwin-specific deps are declared inside =packages.darwin.*= and
=activation.darwin= in the recipe. The Home Manager activation step writes
them to =~/.config/kaizen/darwin-deps.json=; =darwin.nix= reads that file and
merges the values into =homebrew.*= and =system.activationScripts=.

The old =*.darwin.nix= sibling-file pattern is *deprecated and removed*.

#+begin_src nix
# features/mytool.nix — recipe attrset, no options/config/mkIf needed
{ pkgs, lib, ... }:
{
  description = "My tool";
  category    = "dev";

  packages.darwin.casks      = [ "mytool" ];
  packages.darwin.taps       = [ "owner/tap" ];
  packages.darwin.brews      = [ { name = "formula"; } ];
  packages.darwin.brewBundle = ''brew "formula"'';

  activation.darwin.setupMytool = ''echo "setting up mytool"'';
}
#+end_src

* Adding a new feature

1. Create =dotfiles/dot_config/nix/modules/features/<name>.nix= following the
   recipe format above.
2. Declare macOS-specific deps in =packages.darwin.*= and =activation.darwin=.
   The loader applies them only on Darwin — no =lib.optionals pkgs.stdenv.isDarwin=
   needed in the recipe file. No separate =.darwin.nix= file needed.
3. Add an entry to the seed file:
   =dotfiles/dot_config/kaizen/feature-meta.json=.
4. Run =kaizen sync= — =feature-loader.nix= picks up the file automatically.

No changes needed to =manifest.toml=, =options.nix=, =darwin.nix=,
=linux.nix=, or =hosts/*.nix=.

* User extensibility

For users comfortable with Nix. Place files in
=~/.config/kaizen/user-features/=. They are auto-discovered alongside
built-in feature modules.

#+begin_src
~/.config/kaizen/user-features/
  mytools.nix          ← recipe file (same format as built-in features)
#+end_src

=*.nix= files receive ={ pkgs, lib, user ? {}, ... }= and return a recipe attrset.
Declare macOS deps inline using =packages.darwin.*= and =activation.darwin=.

** Legacy: user-features/*.darwin.nix (backward compatibility)

This pattern is preserved for backward compatibility only. The primary contract
for new features is inline darwin deps in =*.nix= via =packages.darwin.*=
and =activation.darwin=.

For user-features (=~/.config/kaizen/user-features/=), =*.darwin.nix= files are
still scanned by =darwin.nix= and remain functional. New user features should
prefer the inline approach.

* kaizen bump

Features declare their bump workflow in the =bump= field of the recipe:

#+begin_src nix
{ ... }:
{
  description   = "Mise toolchains";
  category      = "dev";
  defaultEnable = true;
  bump = {
    before  = [{ run = [ "mise" "install" ]; onFailure = "fail"; }];
    run     = [{ run = [ "~/.config/scripts/mise-bump" ]; onFailure = "fail"; }];
    capture = [ "~/.config/mise.lock" ];
  };
}
#+end_src

The =bump= submodule has three fields:

- =before= — hooks that run before the main bump command.
- =run= — the main bump commands.
- =capture= — paths passed to =chezmoi re-add= after commands complete.

Each hook has a =run= argv list and an optional =onFailure= policy (default: =warn=).

- =onFailure = "warn"= prints a warning and continues.
- =onFailure = "fail"= prints an error and stops the workflow.

Use =--only <feature>= to run the bump workflow for a single feature only
(e.g. =kaizen bump --only mise= or =kaizen bump --only nix-system=).

Features are executed in category order: =dev → system → other → ai=.
dev/toolchain features run first so tools (e.g. =pi= via mise) are upgraded
before AI extension updates that depend on them.

* Infrastructure modules

Modules that are not user-visible features (fonts, darkman, battery thresholds)
live in =dotfiles/dot_config/nix/modules/system/= and are imported explicitly
in =darwin.nix= / =linux.nix=. They are never auto-discovered.
